blogs.title: When the Brainstem Silences the Breath: Chiari I as an Acquired Ondine’s Curse
blogs.description: Explore how Chiari I malformation can produce central hypoventilation that mimics congenital Ondine’s curse. Discuss the neuroanatomy of automatic vs. voluntary breathing, clinical clues (asymptomatic desaturation, lack of dyspnea), diagnostic work‑up (polysomnography, MRI), and the role of posterior fossa decompression in reversing the respiratory failure.

blogs.title: Beyond the Laryngoscope: Recognizing Neurogenic Dysphagia in Chiari I
blogs.description: Detail the presentation of bulbar dysfunction in Chiari I, focusing on equal difficulty swallowing solids and liquids, normal endoscopic findings, and the importance of early neurologic referral. Review swallowing physiology, videofluoroscopic patterns of neurogenic dysphagia, and evidence‑based management, including surgical versus conservative approaches.

blogs.title: Hidden in Plain Sight: The Value of Re‑Reviewing Old Head Imaging for Chiari Diagnosis
blogs.description: Use the case’s missed crowded foramen magnum on a 14‑year‑old CT to illustrate common imaging pitfalls. Provide a step‑by‑step checklist for radiologists and clinicians to spot Chiari I on CT and MRI, discuss when to order dedicated cranio‑cervical imaging, and outline how early detection changes patient outcomes.

blogs.title: Sleep‑Related Breathing Disorders in Chiari I: Central Apnoea, Under‑diagnosis, and the Limits of Type III Studies
blogs.description: Analyze the prevalence of central sleep apnea in Chiari patients, explain why type III home studies can underestimate severity, and argue for full polysomnography with capnography. Include practical guidance on screening, interpreting AHI in the context of brainstem compression, and peri‑operative considerations for decompression surgery.

blogs.title: Trauma‑Triggered Chiari? Disentangling Congenital Versus Acquired Tonsillar Herniation
blogs.description: Discuss the controversial relationship between head injury and Chiari I development. Review literature on secondary Chiari post‑trauma, pathophysiological mechanisms (CSF flow alteration, posterior fossa crowding), and propose a diagnostic algorithm for patients with new‑onset headaches or respiratory symptoms after trauma.

blogs.title: Scalp Allodynia and Vertex Headache in Chiari I: A Window into Occipital Neuralgia and Burning Vertex Syndrome
blogs.description: Examine the rare but intriguing symptom of scalp allodynia relieved by hair cutting. Compare occipital neuralgia, nummular headache, and burning vertex syndrome, and discuss how Chiari I may contribute to these pain syndromes via brainstem and cranial nerve irritation. Offer assessment tools and therapeutic options, including nerve blocks and decompression.
